answer: One effective defense is requiring agents to lock a refundable bond before they can transact. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, with strict rate limits, and only earns higher limits by completing verified work over time. Like an onyx seal, the bond is hard to forge cheaply: creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so an attacker must pay real capital up front. Honest agents get their bond back, while cheaters lose it. The cost scales with the size of the echo chamber an attacker tries to build, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
